additional_surveys.citation: Kenneth Lönnqvist and Minna Lönnqvist, with Reino Anttila (2004), Spatial Approach to the Ruins of Khirbet Qumran at the Dead Sea, ISPRS XXXV, Commission V, pp. 558–563
additional_surveys.duplicate_check: No occurrence of authors, title, ISPRS or URL found in existing research notes before this review.

report_and_photo_followup.citation: Yitzhak Magen and Yuval Peleg, Back to Qumran: Final Report (1993–2004), JSP 18 (2018)
report_and_photo_followup.verified: Full chapter available locally; short and long tunnel descriptions and fissure offsets extracted with source quotations. Figure 82 repeats the underlying 2007 Fig. 35 aerial; not independent map control.
report_and_photo_followup.access_status: Resolved by user upload: 91-page PDF containing JSTOR cover and printed pp. 11–100. Water-system text and relevant figures inspected. See magen2018_extracted.md.
report_and_photo_followup.duplicate_check: Distinct from the 2007 preliminary report already used; no occurrence of the 2018 title/date was found in existing local research notes.
report_and_photo_followup.foldout_lead: A one-page reproduction of the NLI catalogue record describes a detailed site plan in a pocket, an 88 x 57 cm folded sheet. The sheet itself has not been recovered, and inclusion in the JSTOR digital edition is unverified.
report_and_photo_followup.false_positive: That Scribd upload contains one page of catalogue metadata, not the book.
report_and_photo_followup.use: Additional detailed feature descriptions beyond 2007 preliminary report; independence of measurements not established. No new coordinates or increased Copper Scroll identification confidence.

report_and_photo_followup.creator: Peter Pennarts
report_and_photo_followup.verified: Downloaded and visually inspected 609 x 600 image. Stone-lined channel in foreground, two people, distant ruins and broad pale background.
report_and_photo_followup.caption: Archive identifies Jan Glissenaar and a shepherd at the aqueduct between hills and ruins; labels the view westward.
report_and_photo_followup.orientation_caution: The apparent water/Dead Sea background and ruins suggest an eastward view instead. This is a visual inference, not a verified correction; do not assign a camera bearing from the caption alone.
report_and_photo_followup.use: Historical feature-comparison lead only. No camera coordinates, bearing, or correspondence with a specific Ilan–Amit feature established. Image not copied into published atlas.

english_edition_access.status: Resolved by user upload: main English volume, 543 PDF pages; northwest water-inlet text, Plate XI and Fig. 174 inspected. See humbert_english_extracted.md.
english_edition_access.finding: Phase reconstruction of settlement inlet; disputes Locus 132 as a decantation pool; missing feed 700 is reconstructed. Does not supply 2002 survey observations or independent tunnel measurements.
english_edition_access.plates: Architectural plates I–XII present at PDF pp. 141–152. Plate XI grid cells are illustration locators, not geographic control.
english_edition_access.confidence_effect: No coordinates or identification-confidence changes; retain author attribution for phase and function disputes.

report_and_photo_followup.citation: David Stacey, Some Archaeological Observations on the Aqueducts of Qumran, Dead Sea Discoveries 14.2 (2007), pp. 222–243
report_and_photo_followup.access_status: Resolved by user upload, 29 September 2026. Read in full. See source_leads_2026-09-29.md.
report_and_photo_followup.verified: Main aqueduct dated no earlier than Herod, after the 31 BCE earthquake (pp. 222–226, 239). Two upstream stages (p. 228): an earlier run-off channel from below the cliffs, citing Ilan–Amit 2002 Fig. 1 'no. 16 eastward' (n. 28); later the dam and tunnelled cliff aqueduct to the beginning of the earlier channel (n. 30).
report_and_photo_followup.duplicate_check: Distinct from Stacey 2009, 'Three Notes on Qumran', already used for the lost dam.
report_and_photo_followup.limitation: Stacey cites the 2002 English figure. Its point numbers are assumed, not checked, to equal the 1989 Hebrew numbers (point 16 = the bend where the channel leaves the cliff). The 2002 chapter's date for the aqueduct (Herod Archelaus, p. 385) is known only through Stacey n. 3.
report_and_photo_followup.followup: Ilan–Amit 2002, JRA Suppl. 46 pp. 380–386, sold only by email order from J. & L. Humphrey.

direct_primary_recovery.citation: E. W. G. Masterman (1903), Notes on Some Ruins and a Rock-Cut Aqueduct in the Wady Kumran, PEFQS 35(3):264–267
direct_primary_recovery.status: Downloaded five-page PDF, including distributor cover; all article pages read. Feature photograph and measurement page visually checked.
direct_primary_recovery.duplicate_check: Masterman already appeared in feature_investigation.md as an upstream reference. Newly recovered direct text and photo, not a new citation.
direct_primary_recovery.finding: Early description of a traversable tunnel, floor break and south-facing window provides a feature-comparison lead. Later accounts may depend on it; dimensions differ. No coordinate registration or Copper Scroll match established.

bibliographic_corrections.finding: The TOC with aqueduct p. 65 belongs to the earlier English field-notes synthesis, not the 2016 IIIA volume. Do not transfer its pagination to IIIA.
